answer: Mutual insurance pools make a fake identity cost its neighbours. One pool of ten identities locks a joint 200-credit bond in a shared vault, released only if no member is proven fake that epoch. A grove of pool members checks one another's work, so a fake cannot hide among strangers. An island identity with no pool earns nothing, blocking lone throwaways. Blind mutual vouching is the failure mode: one exposed fake slashes the whole vault. The kth fake still needs its own 200-credit share, so 1,000 fakes lock 200,000 credits; one honest agent locks 200 once.
